newsitem.title: SPAIN: TELEFONICA NOT CONCERNED ABOUT SHARE PRICE.
newsitem.headline: TELEFONICA NOT CONCERNED ABOUT SHARE PRICE.

text.p: The finance director of Spain's Telefonica said he was not concerned about the company's rising share price ahead of its share offer, saying in an interview with Reuters Financial Television it would be reasonable.
"The range of 3,300 to 3,400 (pesetas), would be reasonable to manage," he said. "So 3,300 would be a possible share price."
A straw poll of analysts by Reuters last week put the price of the February 18 sale of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake in the telecoms company at between 3,200 to 3,400 pesetas.
Some of the analysts said they were worried that the pre-sale excitement could push up the share price to unattractive levels.
"We don't see that the actual price of the issue will give us any special concern," Telefonica de Espana finance director Alfonso Pajuelo said.
He later told Reuters that it was not good for the share price to rise during the subscription period, which opened on Monday, because it encouraged institutional investors to buy outside the offer.
Most analysts see the retail domestic demand far outstripping the institutional appetite, although the company is generally seen as a good buy at the current prices with a lot of growth potential.
Telefonica rose 70 pesetas to 3,410 at 1215 GMT, a record high, after hitting a record high in early trade as the share subscription period opened.
